# Forkward

> Forkward is a free, private web app for healthier everyday food choices. It includes Pantry Lens (recipes from kitchen photos), a food and drink swaps program, and Reflect AI, a separate studio for conceptual visual studies. Forkward is educational only — not medical, allergen-safety, or food-safety advice.

## Pages

- [Home](https://forkward.com.au/): Overview of Forkward, how Pantry Lens works, and an FAQ.
- [Pantry Lens](https://forkward.com.au/pantry/): Upload up to four fridge, freezer, pantry, cupboard, or bench photos (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC). Confirm a starter ingredient list, add avoid-ingredients and culture cues, then get three practical Australian, Filipino, or AU × Filipino fusion recipe cards plus optional shopping-list gaps. Runs in the browser; it does not guess quantities, expiry dates, allergens, or nutrition.
- [Swaps](https://forkward.com.au/swaps/): "How much if I swapped X for Y" comparisons for beer, potatoes, chips, rice, and pasta. Educational estimates with clear alcohol disclaimers.
- [Reflect AI](https://forkward.com.au/reflect/): Standalone studio — mirror photo upload, routine sliders, and a conceptual "after" preview. Educational visualisation, not a medical prediction.
- [Privacy](https://forkward.com.au/privacy/): Photos stay in-session only, are not uploaded to a Forkward server, and are never written to localStorage. Optional meal prefs stay on the device and can be wiped with "Forget pantry context".

## Guides

- [Guides index](https://forkward.com.au/guides/): Plain-English food guides for Australian kitchens. Educational only, not medical advice.
- [How to turn pantry photos into meals](https://forkward.com.au/guides/pantry-photos-to-meals/): A practical method for turning what's already in your fridge, freezer and pantry into dinner, using photos, a quick ingredient check and a simple meal formula.
- [Healthy Aussie swaps that still feel like a treat](https://forkward.com.au/guides/healthy-aussie-swaps/): Simple everyday swaps for classic Australian foods, from the barbie to the servo pie, that keep the flavour and lift the veg, fibre and wholegrains.
- [Healthier takes on Filipino favourites](https://forkward.com.au/guides/healthy-filipino-favourites/): Keep the flavour of adobo, sinigang, pancit and more while adding vegetables, trimming fat and going easier on salt, with tips that work in an Australian kitchen.
- [High-protein meals on a budget](https://forkward.com.au/guides/high-protein-budget-meals/): Affordable protein sources available at Australian supermarkets and easy meal ideas built around eggs, legumes, tinned fish, tofu and cheaper cuts.
- [How to read food labels in Australia](https://forkward.com.au/guides/reading-food-labels-australia/): A plain-English guide to the Nutrition Information Panel, ingredient lists, Health Star Ratings and date marks on Australian food packaging.
- [Meal prep basics for busy weeks](https://forkward.com.au/guides/meal-prep-basics/): A beginner's approach to meal prep: planning, batch cooking, safe storage and keeping it interesting so the food actually gets eaten.
- [Practical ways to cut back on added sugar](https://forkward.com.au/guides/reducing-sugar/): Where added sugar hides in Australian diets, how to spot it on labels, and easy swaps for drinks, breakfast and snacks.
- [Eating out smarter without missing out](https://forkward.com.au/guides/eating-out-smarter/): Simple strategies for cafes, pubs, takeaway and restaurants: what to look for on the menu and how to balance the plate while still enjoying the meal.
- [Reducing food waste at home](https://forkward.com.au/guides/reducing-food-waste/): Plan, store and use up food better: practical habits that save money and stop good food ending up in the bin.
- [Healthy lunchbox ideas for school and work](https://forkward.com.au/guides/healthy-lunchbox-ideas/): Easy, balanced lunchbox combinations for kids and adults, built around the five food groups and leftovers.
